policy: Explicit editorial study repairs and accepted alternatives. Original text, choices and supplied marks are preserved; no official-key claim.

biochemistry-2025-feb-dds-q004.prompt: Which complication of cystic fibrosis is hepatobiliary, rather than part of its pancreatic, pulmonary or male reproductive manifestations?
biochemistry-2025-feb-dds-q004.explanation: Cholestasis is the hepatobiliary complication. The source EXCEPT question was defective because all four choices can occur in CF. The study stem is narrowed to organ-system classification; D does NOT mean cholestasis is absent in CF.
evidence: https://www.cff.org/medical-professionals/cystic-fibrosis-screening-evaluation-and-management-hepatobiliary-disease

biochemistry-2025-feb-dds-q009.prompt: Persistent hepatic cholesterol accumulation, especially together with excess hepatic triglyceride, can contribute to progression of which listed liver disease?
biochemistry-2025-feb-dds-q009.explanation: Fatty liver disease is the best match to this repaired lipid-accumulation stem. Free-cholesterol lipotoxicity can contribute to steatohepatitis. The original statement of influx exceeding efflux establishes accumulation only; it cannot diagnose a particular disease or prove cholestasis. This is an explanatory study reconstruction, not a recovered official key.
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3186822/
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, cholesterol and lipid metabolism chapters.

biochemistry-2023-july-23-q002.prompt: Which effect of citrate is INDIRECT, through increased malonyl-CoA and inhibition of CPT-I, rather than direct enzyme regulation or export of acetyl units?
biochemistry-2023-july-23-q002.explanation: Inhibition of beta-oxidation is indirect: citrate activates ACC, malonyl-CoA rises, and CPT-I is inhibited. The other choices describe direct PFK-1 inhibition, acetyl-unit export and ACC activation. All four original statements are defensible; adding INDIRECT repairs the EXCEPT item without teaching that citrate has no effect on fatty-acid oxidation.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, chapters 8, 16 and 17; Biochemistry II review: fatty-acid synthesis.

biochemistry-2023-jan-29-q010.explanation: Cellulose synthesis uses UDP-glucose. The original choices omit UDP; choice C is repaired from GDP to UDP. ADP-glucose is the starch donor, not the cellulose donor. The assigned C refers to the repaired choice, not the printed GDP option.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, activated sugar nucleotides; carbohydrate metabolism MD Kish slide deck, carbohydrate biosynthesis section.

optionPatches.A: Inhibiting the reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonate

biochemistry-2022-jan-26-q046.explanation: HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate from HMG-CoA. Its inhibition reduces cholesterol synthesis and promotes hepatic LDL-receptor expression. The supplied A mark is plausible only after repairing the option: inhibiting formation of HMG-CoA would target a different step.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, PDF pp. 410-414.

optionPatches.E: None of the above: all four processes can occur in liver

biochemistry-2017-kish-q010.explanation: Liver can transaminate alanine to pyruvate, form glutamate from alpha-ketoglutarate, perform gluconeogenesis and use glucose for energy. The absent 'none' option has been added; these processes need not all dominate simultaneously in the same nutritional state.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, carbohydrate metabolism, nitrogen metabolism and fed-fast integration chapters.

optionPatches.E: None of the above: all four are non-protein nitrogen compounds

biochemistry-theory-53-q013.explanation: Free glutamine, urate, urea and creatinine all contribute non-protein nitrogen. Glutamine is an amino acid, not a protein. Added E corrects the original EXCEPT question; the supplied A mark is not a valid biochemical distinction.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK305/
Biochemistry II review: renal biochemistry and nonprotein nitrogen.

biochemistry-theory-53-q026.prompt: Which organ also has local creatine-synthesis capacity, despite being omitted from the simplified liver-kidney-muscle creatine diagram?
biochemistry-theory-53-q026.explanation: Brain cells have creatine-synthesis capacity as well as creatine uptake. The supplied C mark cannot mean the brain never synthesizes creatine. The study stem explicitly tests this correction rather than repeating the original false exclusion.
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3355046/
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1175845/

biochemistry-theory-53-q029.prompt: What is the clinical syndrome of systemic manifestations associated with severe retention of nitrogenous waste in kidney failure, as distinct from the laboratory finding azotemia?
biochemistry-theory-53-q029.explanation: Uremia is the clinical syndrome. Azotemia means biochemical elevation of nitrogenous wastes; it is not a synonym. The stem is repaired to preserve the likely intended B while retaining the clinically important distinction.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK305/
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK507821/

optionPatches.C: Reduced UGT1A1 activity causes mild, usually benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia

biochemistry-1403-1404-group-b-q007.explanation: Gilbert syndrome reduces bilirubin glucuronidation, commonly leaving about 30% of normal UGT activity. The ancestry statement is replaced with the established mechanism; ancestry alone is not a diagnostic rule. Toxic hyperbilirubinemia requiring transfusion is not the usual Gilbert phenotype.
evidence: https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/gene/ugt1a1/

biochemistry-1401-metabolism-q010.explanation: Succinyl-CoA synthetase couples succinyl-CoA conversion to succinate to substrate-level phosphorylation, producing GTP in the GDP-forming reaction. The original B arrow is reversed; that direction consumes rather than produces the nucleotide triphosphate.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, TCA-cycle chapter; carbohydrate metabolism MD Kish slide deck, TCA cycle.

optionPatches.D: Increase – usually normal or variable, not a defining diagnostic change

biochemistry-1399-metabolism-q006.explanation: Unconjugated bilirubin rises in Gilbert syndrome. A fixed decrease in urinary urobilinogen is not a reliable defining finding. D is repaired to reflect that limitation; absence of urine bilirubin should not be confused with absence of urobilinogen.
evidence: https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/gene/ugt1a1/
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, bilirubin metabolism; Biochemistry II review: heme and bilirubin disorders.

optionPatches.E: None of the above: all can be true in neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia

biochemistry-1399-metabolism-q009.explanation: Immature hepatic uptake and conjugation both contribute. Unbound unconjugated bilirubin can enter the brain, and phototherapy forms more water-soluble photoisomers. Added E corrects the flawed EXCEPT list; the original D mark would wrongly deny impaired uptake.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK532930/
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, bilirubin metabolism.

biochemistry-1400-clinical-q009.prompt: Which paired biochemical abnormalities characterize SLOS and mevalonic aciduria, respectively?
biochemistry-1400-clinical-q009.explanation: SLOS impairs DHCR7 and raises 7-dehydrocholesterol; mevalonate-kinase deficiency can cause mevalonic aciduria. The original paired hematologic claim could not be substantiated as a reliable discriminator, so this is an explicitly reconstructed biochemical version—not verification of its thrombocytopenia/leukocytosis key.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1143/
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2850914/

optionPatches.E: None of the above: all can occur in cirrhosis

biochemistry-1400-clinical-q019.explanation: Cirrhosis may raise conjugated bilirubin, prolong PT and aPTT and reduce albumin. These changes vary with severity and are not obligatory in every patient. Added E repairs the all-true EXCEPT list; increased conjugated bilirubin is not excluded by cirrhosis.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK482489/

biochemistry-1400-clinical-q022.explanation: Both A (GGT) and C (ALT) are accepted for the exact printed wording. ALT is soluble; GGT is membrane anchored by a transmembrane segment, not a GPI anchor. ALP and ecto-5-prime-nucleotidase are GPI anchored. C is the supplied/preferred teaching key, but marking A wrong would be unjustified.
evidence: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P19440/entry
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P05186/entry
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P21589/entry

optionPatches.C: Increased leucine and branched-chain alpha-keto acids

biochemistry-1400-clinical-q027.explanation: MSUD blocks branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase. Accumulated leucine and its ketoacid contribute to neurotoxicity. The source C has the direction reversed and omits leucine; it is repaired rather than accepting the unsupported ammonia key.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1319/
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, branched-chain amino-acid metabolism.

biochemistry-1400-clinical-q028.prompt: Which listed inherited metabolic disease is classically associated with a maple-syrup or burnt-sugar odor caused by sotolon?
biochemistry-1400-clinical-q028.explanation: MSUD is the established disease association. Sotolon was identified in urine from affected patients. The original NOT-occur list makes unsupported general claims about pregnancy and starvation; the study question instead tests the demonstrated association. Odor alone is not diagnostic and dietary exposure can mimic it.
evidence: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10234605/

biochemistry-1403-clinical-q003.prompt: How many disulfide bonds connect the A and B chains of mature insulin?
biochemistry-1403-clinical-q003.explanation: There are TWO interchain bridges, plus ONE intrachain bridge within the A chain, giving THREE in total. The original choices omit three. Specifying bonds between the chains makes the supplied B (two) correct without teaching the wrong total.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, PDF pp. 562-563.

biochemistry-1403-clinical-q007.prompt: Which listed carbohydrate can be reduced to galactitol and cause cataracts when its metabolism is defective?
biochemistry-1403-clinical-q007.explanation: Galactose is reduced by aldose reductase to galactitol, which accumulates in the lens. The source conflates this polyol mechanism with advanced glycation. The repaired question isolates the cataract mechanism; AGE formation is a separate nonenzymatic process.
evidence: Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition, PDF pp. 230-245.

biochemistry-1403-clinical-q011.explanation: Increased 7-dehydrocholesterol is the characteristic biochemical finding of DHCR7 deficiency. The original anemia/platelet choices are not reliable SLOS diagnostic discriminators. Added E supplies the established missing answer; the printed D mark is retained only as source provenance.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1143/

biochemistry-1403-clinical-q032.prompt: Which listed inherited metabolic disease is classically associated with a maple-syrup or burnt-sugar odor caused by sotolon?
biochemistry-1403-clinical-q032.explanation: MSUD has a demonstrated sotolon-associated odor. The original EXCEPT list does not establish the other claimed associations, so this explicitly repaired version tests the supported positive association. This repair does not authenticate the source A key.
evidence: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10234605/

biochemistry-1403-clinical-q039.prompt: In a patient with dyspnea and a low clinical probability of pulmonary embolism, which fibrin-breakdown marker can help exclude venous thromboembolism when negative in an appropriate diagnostic pathway?
biochemistry-1403-clinical-q039.explanation: D-dimer measures breakdown products of cross-linked fibrin. A negative result can help exclude thromboembolism in appropriately selected patients; a positive result is nonspecific. BNP instead reflects cardiac wall stress and supports heart-failure assessment. The original stem did not distinguish these roles, so the intended clot-related role is now explicit.
evidence: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng158/chapter/recommendations
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK545216/

biochemistry-2021-june-23-izam-q005.explanation: The precise term for elevated blood urate is hyperuricemia. The printed uricemia merely denotes urate in blood; option B is explicitly corrected.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Purines, pyrimidines, salvage and DNA precursor supply
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.

biochemistry-2021-june-23-izam-q026.explanation: Insulin promotes HMG-CoA reductase activity in the fed state. The original blanket EXCEPT wording about cortisol/glucocorticoids is replaced with a direct regulatory question.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Cholesterol, bile acids and steroid synthesis
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.
biochemistry-2021-june-23-izam-q026.prompt: Which listed hormone promotes activation of HMG-CoA reductase in the fed state?

biochemistry-2021-june-23-izam-q027.explanation: B is the compensatory hepatic pathway: loss of bile acids increases conversion of cholesterol to bile acids. Broad source alternatives about excretion/catabolism overlap, so the study stem asks for the specific pathway.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Cholesterol, bile acids and steroid synthesis
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.
biochemistry-2021-june-23-izam-q027.prompt: Which listed hepatic metabolic change compensates for interruption of enterohepatic bile-acid recycling by bile-acid sequestrants?

biochemistry-2021-june-23-izam-q037.explanation: Aerobic glycolysis itself makes 2 ATP and 2 cytosolic NADH: 5 ATP equivalents with the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle or 7 with malate-aspartate, using modern P/O values. None of the four source options correctly gives this; an explicit E is added. Complete glucose oxidation is a different question.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Respiratory chain and transparent ATP accounting
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.

optionPatches.E: 5 or 7 ATP equivalents, depending on the cytosolic NADH shuttle

biochemistry-2024-july-13-izam-q033.explanation: Ribonucleotide reductase supplies deoxyribonucleotide precursors and therefore contributes indirectly to dTMP production. The source D wording is too broad to call false. D is explicitly changed to a false direct-enzyme claim; thymidylate synthase, not RNR, directly methylates dUMP.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Purines, pyrimidines, salvage and DNA precursor supply
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.

optionPatches.D: Directly converts dUMP into dTMP by methylation

biochemistry-2024-dec-05-izam-q020.explanation: FMN has the lowest reduction potential among the listed respiratory carriers. The ambiguous phrase tendency to oxidize is clarified to oxidizing power.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Respiratory chain and transparent ATP accounting
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.

biochemistry-2024-dec-05-izam-q023.explanation: CETP transfers neutral lipids between lipoproteins and can interact with triglyceride-rich particles. It is not an obligatory component of the canonical ApoC-II/LPL hydrolysis step; the original broad assertion that it has no role is avoided.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Micelles, enterocytes, chylomicrons and remnant uptake
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.
biochemistry-2024-dec-05-izam-q023.prompt: Which listed factor is NOT required for the canonical ApoC-II-activated LPL hydrolysis of chylomicron triglycerides, with HDL serving as an apoprotein donor?

biochemistry-undated-50-izam-q013.explanation: The original non-thiazide antihypertensive category is too broad (loop diuretics and some other drugs can increase urate). D is repaired to losartan, which can lower serum urate.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459284/

optionPatches.D: Losartan, an angiotensin II receptor blocker with a uricosuric effect

biochemistry-undated-50-izam-q014.explanation: ADA deficiency causes one form of SCID, not every SCID. The source is narrowed to that form; lymphopenia, not lymphocytosis, is expected.
evidence: Biochemistry II review: Purines, pyrimidines, salvage and DNA precursor supply
Ferrier, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 6th edition; corresponding pathway chapter.
biochemistry-undated-50-izam-q014.prompt: All of the following statements about untreated ADA-deficiency SCID are correct, EXCEPT:

biochemistry-undated-50-izam-q015.explanation: Ferrochelatase deficiency causes erythropoietic protoporphyria. Photosensitivity depends on the acute hepatic porphyria subtype and is absent in acute intermittent porphyria, making the original blanket EXCEPT stem unsafe.
evidence: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK22229/
biochemistry-undated-50-izam-q015.prompt: Which statement identifies the enzyme defect of erythropoietic protoporphyria, rather than an acute hepatic porphyria?
